## Overview

This Adyen account-structure guide describes the hierarchy of one company account, one or more merchant accounts, optional account groups for multiple merchant accounts, and optional stores under merchant accounts for point-of-sale locations. It explains which level holds users and invoices, processes payments and receives payouts/reconciliation reports, or groups user access. The raw page was last modified 2023-10-19 and captured 2026-09-15. See [[adyen]] and [[adyen-account-structure]].

## Key takeaways

- A business has a single **company account** and one or more **merchant accounts** underneath. The company account represents the core business to Adyen, holds merchant accounts and users, and receives the monthly invoice by default. For POS, one or more stores may sit under each merchant account to represent physical locations; the linked in-person guide owns store setup details.
- **Merchant accounts** are the sub-accounts in which payments are processed. The guide locates payout receipt and reconciliation reports there, along with configuration of payment methods, processing currencies, and overrides of company-level risk rules. A single merchant account is enough for many customers; multiple accounts can be useful or required depending on the business. Its Europe/US tea-shop example illustrates a possible split, not a mandatory geography rule.
- When there are multiple merchant accounts, **account groups** provide an optional user-access layer. Subject to user roles, users may search payments and view/download reports across the group's merchant accounts. The page says one merchant account may belong to only one account group. It gives country/region and brand grouping as examples, not required designs.
- This account hierarchy is not a determination of legal entity, merchant of record, contractual liability, beneficiary ownership, platform organization structure, or end-to-end funds flow. In particular, the page's merchant-account payout location does not establish who legally sells to the shopper or owns proceeds. The linked structure-selection and management pages are needed for their respective procedures.

quotes.text: With Adyen, you have a single [company account](#company-account), and one or more sub-accounts called [merchant accounts](#merchant-accounts). If you have several merchant accounts, you can additionally group them together in [account groups](#account-groups).

Your company account represents your core business entity with us. The company account holds all your merchant accounts and [users](/account/users), and is where your [monthly invoice](/reporting/invoice-reconciliation/payment-processing-invoice) is issued to by default.

Your payments are processed in sub-accounts called merchant accounts. The merchant account is where you receive the payout of funds, as well as the reports used for [reconciliation](/reporting/settlement-reconciliation). It is also where you configure payment methods, processing currencies, and override risk management rules set at company level.

Account groups provide an additional layer to manage your company account in case you have several merchant accounts. By grouping several merchant accounts into an account group, you can give users access to all merchant accounts in that group. ## Overview

Adyen's account-structure guide describes one company account with one or more merchant accounts, optional account groups when several merchant accounts exist, and optional stores under merchant accounts for in-person locations. This is an account and access hierarchy, not by itself a merchant-of-record, legal-entity, contractual-liability, ownership, or full funds-flow model.

## Account levels

The company account represents the core business to Adyen, holds merchant accounts and users, and receives the monthly invoice by default. Merchant accounts process payments and are where the guide locates payouts and reconciliation reports; payment methods, processing currencies, and overrides of company-level risk rules are configured there. The guide says one merchant account is enough for many customers, while more may be useful or required depending on their business. Its regional example is illustrative.

With multiple merchant accounts, account groups can grant role-qualified users access to search payments and view/download reports across grouped merchant accounts. A merchant account may belong to only one group. For point-of-sale payments, stores can be placed under merchant accounts to represent physical locations; separate in-person documentation owns store-setup details. Account grouping is not evidence that merchant-account payouts combine.

## Evidence boundary

This is a 2023-last-modified Adyen page captured 2026-09-15. It does not identify the legal seller or merchant of record, establish an organization entity, decide current account eligibility, or prove a live payout or payment outcome. Use the source and linked selection/management guides for applicable setup details.
